methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $254M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 1 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Black Semiconductor, a Series A chip design company founded by Daniel and Sebastian Schall, has raised €254.4M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 12 private-sector peers in Chips & Semiconductors (including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor) plus 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised (€254.4M) as a proxy for Series A valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of €509M. Peer-median analysis could not be deployed: while 12 same-sector peers exist, only 1–2 fell within narrow same-stage or adjacent-stage filters, below the minimum threshold of 3 datapoints needed for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring via the 21.5x P/S median across the three public tickers is inapplicable without disclosed revenue figures.

The single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of €432M (low) to €585M (high), with a median of €509M. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue disclosure, which precludes public-comp calibration, and the thin peer dataset at this specific stage, limiting cross-validation. Revenue traction and IP defensibility will be material to any Series B repricing.
